html:
A forced swap of peoples agreed by Greece and Turkey in 1923. About 1.6 million people were moved: roughly 1.2 million Orthodox Christians from Turkey to Greece and some 400,000 Muslims from Greece to Turkey.

It followed the Greco-Turkish War, which ended with the defeat of the Greek army in Anatolia and the burning of Smyrna in 1922. Most Greeks of western Anatolia had already fled. The agreement, signed at Lausanne in January 1923, made the moves compulsory and final.

People were sorted by religion, not language. Many Orthodox who spoke only Turkish were sent to Greece, and many Greek speaking Muslims to Turkey. The Greeks of Istanbul and the Muslims of Western Thrace were exempt.

The exchange ended some 3,000 years of Greek life in Anatolia. Greece, a small and poor country, had to absorb a fifth of its population in new arrivals. It came in the same year as the founding of the Republic of Turkey, out of the old Ottoman Empire.
sum: A forced swap of peoples agreed by Greece and Turkey in 1923. About 1.6 million people were moved: roughly 1.2 million Orthodox Christians from Turkey to Greece and some 400,000 Muslims from Greece to Turkey.
